attribution.note: Marcus states and endorses the claim in his own prose.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the categorical scope and mimicry assertion. Reading this as an observation through publication fits the surrounding discussion.

contract.note: The contract supplies an ordinary, contextually fair reading of proper world models and mimicry. It reasonably requires robust use without demanding perfection, though Marcus supplied no operational threshold.

evidence.note: Timely benchmark evidence establishes selected world-modeling weaknesses, but cannot establish universal absence or explain all capabilities as mimicry.
Relevant spatial and temporal representations are demonstrated. Their use for causal inference and prediction remains explicitly unproven.
Causal interventions establish entity-attribute binding, challenging a simple surface-matching account. Binding alone does not establish the robust world-state updating required by the contract.

Entity tracking provides material counterevidence, but the reported behavior does not establish robust world-model use under the contract. Specialized fine-tuning results cannot independently settle the claim.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes both substantial failures and meaningful representational and tracking abilities. Failures cannot prove the universal claim, while the positive findings do not demonstrate a qualifying robust world model in a general-purpose LLM. Neither resolution condition is met.
